chapter_title: Concerning the Interpretation of the Fourteen [Great Aeons] of Light, about which Sethel has spoken in [his Prayer]
chapter_note: The chapter opens with a clear dialogue-frame request (disciples → apostle) and a brief promise-to-interpret. The core teaching appears as a compact, systematic fourteenfold enumeration (5+2+5+2), with cosmos→cosmos mapping (aeons/elements/sons/call-hearing/fathers) and an impersonal explanatory voice. The final paragraph preserves substantial cosmological teaching about the hidden land/plenitude and the Ambassador’s kingship, but is introduced through an interpretive link to Seth’s prayer; that Seth-prayer linkage is likely a later editorial anchoring to a gnostic tradition rather than the oldest substrate.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic dialogue frame: disciples question, honorific address (“our master”), request to be enlightened, and explicit anchoring to a named written source (“prayer of Sethel”). This is editorial apparatus wrapping the teaching.
Dialogue attribution (“Then the enlightener speaks…”) plus a promissory interpretive line. No cosmological exposition yet; functions as narrative linkage into the teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: Happen you know this, that the [ ... ] below abide in fourteen [great aeons ...]: the five elements, the sons of the First Man, together with the call and the hearing. They anoint them, living in them. These shall make seven, five plus two.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic enumeration and degree-structure arithmetic (five plus two) within the Manichaean cosmic system (elements/sons of the First Man/Call/Hearing). Impersonal explanatory voice; no citation formula or institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... the] f[ive s]ons of the Living Spirit who [support] all [the wei]ght of the universe; together with the [Li]vi[ng] Spirit [and the Fir]st Man, their fathers. These are the fourt[een p]raises that he has proclaimed, the praise that is made of fourteen pra[yers], by which the universe is established.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Completes the 14-structure (5 sons + 2 fathers) and grounds it cosmologically (“support… weight of the universe… universe is established”). The “fourteen prayers/praises” language reads as an internal cosmological-liturgical mechanism rather than church instruction.

paragraphs.core_text: for they are expl[ai]ned [ ... the la]nd that is not revealed. This land [ ... ... is estab]lished. They bore up under the enemy [ ... ... equa]ls them. The hidden plenitude that [ ... ] the Ambassador who came from the Father, the [ ... ] He came and stood firm in the midst of these [ ... ]: he is called the good father of [all] the ae[ons and gods] who are holy and conjoined. He has become leader and a great king after the likeness of the first Father, the lord of all these cou[nse]ls. This universe is held together by their will [ ... ] to the end of all things.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the introductory interpretive anchoring to Seth and his prayer ("[There are fourt]een aeons of light [ ... ] of Seth [e] ... ] about them in his prayer,") as an editorial linkage to an external named source/tradition; retained the ensuing cosmological exposition about the hidden land/plenitude and the Ambassador’s role, which stays within the cosmic system.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core cosmological myth/exposition (hidden land/plenitude; Ambassador-from-the-Father; cosmic kingship; universe held together by their will) is present, but it is front-loaded with an editorial move that grounds the teaching in Seth’s written prayer—an external textual anchor characteristic of later compilation and tradition-linking.
